Test: geographic outliers

Source: R/clean.R, R/test-docs.R
test_outlier.Rd

Flags records far from the other records of their species. For each record the haversine distances (km) to the species' other records are computed, leaving out zero distances (the record itself and records at the same point); a record is flagged when its mean distance lies above the upper fence of the species' mean distances: Q75 + mltpl x IQR (method = "quantile") or median + mltpl x MAD ("mad"). With method = "distance" a record is flagged when its nearest other record is more than tdi km away. Species with fewer than min_occs distinct points are not tested.

Usage

clean_outlier(
  x,
  method = "quantile",
  mltpl = 5,
  tdi = 1000,
  min_occs = 7,
  thinning = FALSE,
  thinning_res = 0.5,
  sampling_thresh = 0,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A data frame of occurrence records.

method, mltpl, tdi, min_occs, thinning, thinning_res, sampling_thresh

Options of the test, as in Settings; the defaults are in the usage line.

...

Further arguments to flag_occurrences(): columns, reference, gazetteers, land_scale.

Value

clean_<test>(): the rows of x the test does not flag, with the columns of x unchanged. See keep_unflagged(), Cleaning functions.

Details

Species with 10,000 records or more, and every species when thinning = TRUE, are tested on a raster approximation: records are counted on a grid of thinning_res degrees spanning all valid records (widened by two cells), distances are taken between cell centres, and the records of the outlier cells are flagged. Without thinning, distances are weighted by the product of the cell counts and a cell's distance to itself counts as 100 x thinning_res / 2 km, as in CoordinateCleaner.

The test needs every record of a species, so it runs in a group pass over the whole input before the record tests; on streamed input that pass reads all files, and a species spread over several files is tested as one.

Fields

lon, lat, species. Records with invalid coordinates are left out.

Settings

settings = list(outlier = list(...)) with method ("quantile"), mltpl (5), tdi (1000 km), min_occs (7), thinning (FALSE), thinning_res (0.5 degrees) and sampling_thresh (0).

Sampling correction

With sampling_thresh above 0, an outlier stays flagged only in a country whose record density (log records per 100 km2) lies above that quantile of the densities of all countries, so that isolated records in poorly sampled countries are kept. The records per country come from gazetteers = list(sampling = <data frame>), with an ISO alpha-2 country column and a records column, for example from rgbif::occ_count() or a tally of the input itself; country areas are computed from the country polygons of the reference.

CoordinateCleaner

Equivalent to cc_outl(); identical flags for species below 10,000 records. In CoordinateCleaner 3.0.1 the raster approximation (10,000 records or more, or thinning = TRUE) flags no records; here the records of the outlier cells are flagged. CoordinateCleaner's sampling correction queries GBIF record counts online at run time; here the counts are a table given with the call, so the flags can be reproduced.

See also

flag_occurrences(), flag_tests()

Other tests: clean_age_equal(), clean_age_outlier(), clean_age_range_outlier(), clean_aohi(), clean_basis_fossil(), clean_capital(), clean_centroid(), clean_country_mismatch(), clean_dataset_ddmm(), clean_dataset_rounded(), clean_duplicate(), clean_equal(), clean_establishment_introduced(), clean_gbif_headquarters(), clean_institution(), clean_invalid(), clean_issue_coordinate(), clean_range(), clean_sea(), clean_sea_nonmarine(), clean_spatiotemporal_outlier(), clean_urban(), clean_zero()

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- data.frame(species = "a", decimalLongitude = c(rnorm(50, 10, 1), 60),
                decimalLatitude = c(rnorm(50, 50, 1), 10))
which(flag_occurrences(x, tests = "outlier")$flag_outlier)
nrow(clean_outlier(x, mltpl = 3))
